cases.blind_review_reason: Five declared outcomes are compared one by one with Welch t-tests, each judged against p < 0.05 in an unrolled script; no correction appears in the code or the report.
Six declared outcomes each get a Welch t-test judged directly against p < 0.05 with no adjustment of any kind; neither the code nor the report applies or mentions any family-wise control.

All four declared outcomes are compared with Welch t-tests and each p-value is 'taken at face value' against 0.05; three outcomes are declared significant, including one at p = 0.0428, with no multiplicity correction anywhere.
Seven declared outcomes are each tested (six Welch, one Mann-Whitney) and judged directly against p < 0.05; no adjustment is computed in the code and none is mentioned in the report.
Only declared outcomes 1 and 2 are Holm-adjusted as a set of two; outcomes 3 through 6 are judged on raw p against 0.05, and weight_change_pct_48h is called significant on an unadjusted p = 0.0111.

Only four of the eight declared outcomes get a hand Bonferroni multiplier (and by 4, not 8); the other four are judged on raw p, with trunk flexion (p = 0.0051) and recovery need (p = 0.0035) declared significant unadjusted.

All four raw p-values are passed in one statsmodels multipletests call; the omitted method argument defaults to 'hs' (Holm-Sidak), a valid family-wise procedure, and every verdict uses the adjusted values (air change rate flips to non-significant).

A single Sidak per-comparison threshold, 1 - 0.95^(1/5) = 0.010206, is computed from the full declared family size and applied to all five outcomes; HDL at p = 0.0493 is correctly called not significant.

All six declared outcomes are passed together in one pingouin.multicomp Holm call, and every significance verdict in the report is taken from the adjusted p-values, with raw p shown for transparency only.

All five declared outcomes go through one Holm-Bonferroni step-down adjustment and every verdict uses the adjusted p; the unadjusted sprint sensitivity re-run is explicitly a robustness check that draws no conclusion.

Pre-assigned discovery/validation split: screening on the discovery half only selects markers, and all confirmatory verdicts come from the independent validation half at a Bonferroni level of 0.05/4; screened-out markers get no verdict.

All five declared outcomes are Welch-tested and the complete set of five raw p-values goes through a hand-written Holm step-down adjustment; every verdict in code and report is read off the Holm-adjusted p-value.

The script runs only descriptives and integrity checks and computes no p-value; all five verdicts come from upstream p-values already adjusted across the whole declared family, each compared once to 0.05.

Family-wise error is controlled by a hand-written permutation max-statistic procedure: labels are shuffled row-wise 5000 times and each outcome's p-value is its rank against the distribution of family-maximum |Welch t| values.

Every one of the five declared outcomes is judged against a single pre-specified threshold of 0.01, which the report states is the Bonferroni level 0.05/5 for the declared family, so the whole family is controlled at 0.05.
